builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: AdaStep: Adaptive Step Credit Weighting for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: AdaStep replaces coarse trajectory-level outcome rewards in RL training of long-horizon LLM agents with a shrinkage-weighted combination of step-level local advantages, where a per-state coefficient derived from an MSE formulation preserves credit attributable to the action and suppresses credit dominated by downstream randomness. It costs only lightweight scalar computation, requiring no critic network, no extra rollouts, and no additional model inference. It can fail if the conditional sampling assumption underlying the optimal shrinkage derivation does not hold in the target environment, or if the group-derived local advantage estimates are too noisy for the signal-to-variance weighting to be meaningful.
rationale: The method is a cheap, additive modification to an existing agentic RL training loop, but it only matters for teams already doing RL post-training of agents, which on a single 24 GB GPU is viable only at small model scale and therefore requires workload-specific validation before adoption.
technique: Adaptive step-credit weighting for agentic RL

It costs only lightweight scalar computation, requiring no critic network, no extra rollouts, and no additional model inference. It can fail if the conditional sampling assumption underlying the optimal shrinkage derivation does not hold in the target environment, or if the group-derived local advantage estimates are too noisy for the signal-to-variance weighting to be meaningful.
The abstract reports consistent improvements over baselines across three model backbones on ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld at low computational cost, but provides no quantified figure.
